questions.question: The marked price of a bed sheet is ₹500. At the time of its sale, two successive discounts of 10% and 5% are available. Find the selling price (in ₹) of the bed sheet.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Convert the successive discount percentages directly into multiplying fractions.

10% discount means selling at 90% ⇒ fraction is 9/10.

5% discount means selling at 95% ⇒ fraction is 19/20.

SP = MP × fraction₁ × fraction₂

SP = 500 × (9/10) × (19/20) = 500 × (171/200)

SP = 2.5 × 171 = 427.50

**∴ The correct answer is ₹427.50.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b429849f3df804496a2e98dc01f4fca757175ec897a90dd2024e832ce2a963d7.png] 

**Given:**

Marked Price (MP) = ₹500

First discount (D₁) = 10%

Second discount (D₂) = 5%

**Formula Used:**

Selling Price (SP) = MP × (1 − D₁/100) × (1 − D₂/100)

**Calculations:**

⇒ SP = 500 × (1 − 10/100) × (1 − 5/100)

⇒ SP = 500 × (90/100) × (95/100)

⇒ SP = 500 × 0.90 × 0.95

⇒ SP = 450 × 0.95

⇒ SP = 450 × (1 − 0.05)

⇒ SP = 450 − 22.50 = 427.50

**∴ The correct answer is ₹427.50.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Equivalent Single Discount Formula

If two successive discounts of x% and y% are allowed, the equivalent single discount is given by: D = [x + y − (x × y) / 100]%.

Marked Price vs Cost Price

Marked Price (MP) is always set above Cost Price (CP) to allow for discounts while still maintaining a profit. Discounts are always calculated on MP, whereas Profit or Loss is calculated on CP.

Successive Percentage Changes

When any value undergoes multiple percentage changes successively, the final value can be found directly by multiplying the base value with the successive compounding factors: Final Value = Base Value × (1 ± R₁/100) × (1 ± R₂/100).

questions.question: A salesman marks his goods 30% above the cost and gives a discount of 10% on them. Find his gain or loss percentage.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A salesman marks his goods 30% above the cost and gives a discount of 10% on them.

**Calculation:**

Let the cost price of the goods be 100x

So, the marked price of the goods = 100x × 1.3 = 130x

Selling price of the goods = 130x × 0.9 = 117x

So, profit = 117x - 100x = 17x

Profit % = (17x)/(100x) times 100 = 17

**∴ The required answer is 17% gain.**

questions.question: An item with a marked price of Rs. 1,940 was sold at a discount of 15%. At what price (in Rs.) was the item sold?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

MP = Rs. 1940

Discount = 15%

Formula:

Discount = (MP - SP) over MP

Calculation:- 

According to the question,

⇒ (15)/(100) = (1940 - SP)/(1940)

⇒ 1940 × 15 = (1940 - SP) × 100

⇒ 1940 × 15 = 1940 × 100 - SP × 100

⇒ SP × 100 = 1940 × 100 - 1940 × 15 

⇒ SP = 1940 × (100 - 15)/100

⇒ SP = 1940 × 85/100 = Rs. 1649

∴ The selling price of the item is Rs. 1,649.

Where S.P. = Selling price, C.P. = Cost price

30% Discount on marked price =( 30/100 )× 100 = Rs30.

⇒ (100 - 30) = Rs 70.

Now, According to the given Question ,

S.P. of retailer = M.P. 

Hence, S.P. of retailer = Rs100. and C.P. = Rs70.

Hence, Profit = (S.P.- C.P.) = (100 -70) = Rs30.

⇒ Profit% = (Profit/C.P.) × 100

⇒ ( 30/70) × 100 = (300/7) % = 42 (6)/(7) %.

**∴ Profit% is 42(6)/(7)** %**.**

questions.question: A discount series of 10% and 16% on an invoice is the same as a single discount of:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The equivalent single discount for two successive discounts a% and b% is:

⇒ Equivalent Discount = a + b − (a × b) / 100

Here, a = 10 and b = 16

⇒ Equivalent Discount = 10 + 16 − (10 × 16) / 100

⇒ Equivalent Discount = 26 − 1.6 = 24.4%

**∴ The correct answer is 24.4%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

First discount = 10%

Second discount = 16%

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/05e66228f63222d4c0ce2faf1b427576aaf1931f64e50e76b13af7a4841e9c68.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let Marked Price (MP) = 100

⇒ Price after 1st discount (10%) = 100 − 10 = 90

⇒ Price after 2nd discount (16%) = 90 − (16 / 100) × 90 = 90 − 14.4 = 75.6

⇒ Total Discount = MP − Selling Price (SP) = 100 − 75.6 = 24.4

⇒ Equivalent single discount percentage = 24.4%

**∴ The correct answer is 24.4%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Ratio Method for Successive Discounts

Convert each discount into a fraction (e.g., 10% = 1/10 ⇒ MP : SP = 10 : 9). Multiply the MP parts and SP parts separately to find the overall ratio, then calculate the total net discount percentage.

Three Successive Discounts

To find the equivalent discount for a%, b%, and c%, first apply the formula a + b − (ab / 100) to find an intermediate discount d%, then apply it again with d% and c%.

Customer vs Dealer Perspective

For a customer, a higher successive discount is better. Among different combinations with the same sum (e.g., 20% + 10% vs 25% + 5%), the one with the larger difference between the individual discounts gives a greater net discount.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Effective Successive Discount

When two successive discounts of d₁% and d₂% are given, the equivalent single discount percentage can be calculated directly using the formula: [d₁ + d₂ − (d₁ × d₂)/100]%.

Marked Price vs Selling Price

A discount is always offered on the Marked Price (MP) of an item. The price obtained after deducting the discount is the final Selling Price (SP). The fundamental formula connects them as SP = MP − Discount.

Relation between CP and MP

If a profit of P% is made by a shopkeeper even after allowing a discount of D%, then the direct ratio between the Cost Price (CP) and the Marked Price (MP) is given by CP/MP = (100 − D)/(100 + P).

questions.question: Rohini buys a Bluetooth headphone set for ₹1,700 from a wholesale shop and marks it at ₹2,000. Later on, she allows a discount of 40% on its sale. What is her loss or gain percentage (correct up to two decimal places)?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price & Discount

Discount is fundamentally an allowance offered to a buyer, always calculated on the Marked Price (MP). Hence, SP = MP − Discount.

Profit & Loss Percentage

Unless otherwise stated, Profit or Loss percentage is strictly calculated with respect to Cost Price (CP). Loss% = (Loss ÷ CP) × 100.

Direct Relation between CP and MP

A rapid formula linking CP and MP directly is: CP ÷ MP = (100 − Discount%) ÷ (100 − Loss%). It bypasses solving for SP.

questions.question: During a new-year sale, a shopkeeper offers a discount scheme to his customers, 'Buy 5 Sweaters, Get 2 Sweaters Free'. Find the effective percentage discount given by the shopkeeper.

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In any Buy X, Get Y Free scheme, the discount percentage is calculated on total items.

Discount % = (Free Items ÷ Total Items) × 100

Here, Free Items = 2 and Total Items = 5 + 2 = 7

⇒ Discount % = (2 ÷ 7) × 100 = 28⁴/₇%

**∴ The correct answer is 28⁴/₇%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Items paid for = 5 sweaters

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c1230fdff6dd40dc4f171b1e4307ca45ba1599f078fda725e6e9fd15c12d6df3.png]

⇒ Discount given = Total MP − SP = 70 − 50 = ₹20

Successive Discounts

When two discounts of a% and b% are given successively, the effective single discount is (a + b − ab ÷ 100)%.

Marked Price & Selling Price

Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price (MP). The final Selling Price (SP) = MP × (100 − Discount%) ÷ 100.

Dishonest Dealer Concept

If a dealer claims to sell goods at Cost Price but uses a false weight, his Profit % = (Error ÷ True Value) × 100.
